key_insight: Knee3DVLM combines full-volume DESS and fluid-sensitive TSE MRI to better capture complementary information for structured knee osteoarthritis assessment.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more comprehensive and standardized knee MRI reporting by predicting anatomically specific MOAKS-derived findings across multiple structures.
method: Dual-sequence vision-language model trained on full-volume knee MRI
Predicts 57 binary diagnostic targets mapped to MOAKS
Compared DESS-only, TSE-only, and fused DESS-TSE setups on subject-disjoint cohorts
evidence_signal: On 1,074 held-out examinations, the fused model achieved the best reported performance: 72.98% average accuracy, 71.17% balanced accuracy, 78.96% mean ROC-AUC, and 78.74% macro ROC-AUC.
watch_item: Performance gains are promising, but clinical translation will depend on external validation, robustness across scanners and protocols, and safe integration into workflow.
paper_title: Knee3DVLM: Dual-Sequence Full-Volume Vision-Language Modeling for Comprehensive Knee MRI Assessment
